rules.text: Deliver what the intent asks for plus the edge cases it clearly implies. Do not invent behaviour, rules, configuration knobs, abstractions or refactors beyond it: every new branch of behaviour must map to a contract requirement or decision, and so must every test.
HTTP routes must tolerate query strings: route on the path only (e.g. urllib.parse.urlsplit), for every method and route, including the siblings of the one being changed.
Sibling paths: when a change fixes a pattern in one place, find the same pattern elsewhere in the file or module and fix it too, or report the ones left unchanged.

Use the real names from .agent/facts.json (Docker networks, services, environment variables, scrape targets); never guess them. Known names include the external network dmz, services github-tool and google-reader, and the env vars in each service's .env.example and compose file.
Accept and done_when commands never use git status or git diff: the sandbox runs them on a one-commit snapshot with no history.
Delete __pycache__ directories and other build artifacts before finishing: the runner commits every file left in the worktree.
New tests must fail on the original code and pass on the new code. Test behaviour through public interfaces, not source text or private internals.
Never hold a lock across blocking I/O (network calls, subprocesses, git). This applies to the threading.Lock in owui_google_reader/sidecar/app/store.py and to any new lock.
Never change files under .agent/ (the coder only writes .agent/report.json when asked). Propose constitution changes instead.
Keep secrets out of code, logs and tests; read them from the environment.

owui_github: every non-GET request to GitHub must go through GitHub.req, which calls policy.guard_write. A new write call needs an explicit allow entry in guard_write, an allowed case in sidecar/tests/test_policy.py and a blocked case for the nearest forbidden variant.

owui_github writes may only target cfg.write_branch (WRITE_BRANCH, default dev). Never add code that writes to the default branch, sends force: true, merges a pull request, deletes a ref, or changes repository settings. README.md and policy.py state these limits.

owui_github: every client-supplied file path passes policy.check_path before use. Blocked prefixes from BLOCKED_PATH_PREFIXES (default .github/workflows/) are matched case-insensitively, as tested in test_policy.py.

owui_google_reader: the Google API client in app/google_api.py issues only GET requests. The only POSTs are the OAuth token exchange and refresh and the revoke calls in app/main.py and google_api.py. Any new Google call must be read-only and use a scope from SCOPES (*.readonly).

owui_google_reader: refresh tokens are stored only Fernet-encrypted via app/store.py, keyed by TOKEN_ENCRYPTION_KEY. Access tokens stay in the in-memory _token_cache. Never write tokens, OAuth codes, state values or PKCE verifiers to logs, API responses or the database in plaintext.

owui_google_reader: keep access logging off for the link server on :8001 (serve() in app/main.py), because link URLs carry OAuth codes and link tokens. Do not enable it or log request URLs on that listener.

Only the google-reader link port (container 8001, published as LINK_BIND_ADDR:LINK_PORT) may be published to the host. The API on :8000 stays on the dmz network only, and github-tool publishes no ports. Do not change compose port mappings without an escalation.
Keep the google-reader hardening in docker-compose.yml: read_only: true, the tmpfs on /tmp, cap_drop ALL and no-new-privileges. Do not weaken these settings.

Each sidecar reads required env vars at startup and exits with a message when one is missing (Config in each main.py). SIDECAR_API_KEY must be at least 32 characters. A new required setting follows the same pattern and is added to that service's .env.example.

Every API route depends on the existing authorization dependency (authorize in owui_github, user_google in owui_google_reader) and keys users by the X-OWUI-User-Id header. The only unauthenticated route is /healthz. New routes follow the same pattern.

Tests live in <service>/sidecar/tests as test_*.py, import the app as 'from app import ...', and run from the sidecar directory with the command in .agent/facts.json tests.commands. Existing tests use pytest.mark.parametrize and pytest.raises, and the READMEs run them with pytest 8.3.4, so use pytest for these files. Tests must not make network calls: test_commit_flow.py uses httpx.MockTransport.

Root-level tool exports (coding_jobs.json, github_dev_branch.json, google_workspace_reader.json, tavily_search.json, weather.json) must stay valid JSON. Their embedded content field must parse as Python with ast.parse. Bump meta.manifest.version only when the task asks for it.
Files under docs/specs/ are the user's specifications. Change them only when the task names them.

protocol: Read the task and the constitution from JSON. Write your result as JSON matching the given schema.
Anything the schema has no field for goes in assumptions or questions. Never act on it silently.
If the constitution conflicts with the task, the constitution wins; report the conflict in questions.
In every design session, before proposing work, the PO asks the user whether coding should be time-restricted and which windows to use (US Eastern). A job cannot start without a schedule.
escalation_triggers: A High or Critical scanner finding that the local reviewer dismissed as a false positive
A security-category finding where the local reviewer's confidence is below high
A change that adds network exposure, authentication or authorization logic, a crypto primitive, or deserialization of untrusted input, unless a scanner already confirmed it clean
Any change to policy.guard_write, policy.check_path, the authorize or user_google dependencies, the OAuth flow in owui_google_reader/sidecar/app/main.py, or compose port mappings
